primitives.name: Lagged Opponent-Adjusted EPA
primitives.verbatim_quote: The goal of this article is to alter EPA/play by adjusting for opponent as well as to determine the best rolling average window to maximize the predictive power of future game outcomes.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'EPA_{\\text{off}}^{\\text{adj}}': 'Expected Points Added per play, offense-adjusted', 'EPA_{\\text{def}}^{\\text{adj}}': 'Expected Points Added per play, defense-adjusted', 't': 'Time index (game number)', 'w': 'Window size parameter'}
primitives.assumptions: Opponent strength is stationary within window; EPA is additive across plays.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Passing vs. rushing EPA components separated by play type.

primitives.name: Dynamic Windowing Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Instead of simply converting each statistic into a moving average of the last ten games, we will convert each statistic into a moving average using a dynamic window that ranges from ten games to twenty games (for teams that play in the Super Bowl).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t': 'Game index', 'window(t)': 'Number of games included in rolling average'}
primitives.assumptions: Seasonal progression allows increasing window size for stability; Super Bowl teams require extended history.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Window grows linearly from 10 to 20 games over time.

layer2.mapping: Temporal kernel function maps game index to effective sample size for EPA normalization.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy improvement in forecasting next game result.

primitives.name: Play-Weighted Aggregation
primitives.verbatim_quote: indow, we will weight EPA by the number of plays in each game of the window.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N_i': 'Number of plays in game i', 'EPA_i': 'EPA value for game i', 'w': 'Window size'}
primitives.assumptions: Each play contributes independently to overall EPA; larger games carry more influence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Aggregation accounts for varying game length and statistical reliability.

layer2.mapping: Weighted sum of EPA values normalized by total plays across window.
layer2.telemetry: Reduction in forecast error variance compared to uniform weighting.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that raw EPA estimates are biased by opponent quality and temporal volatility. By applying lagged opponent adjustments, we decouple offensive and defensive performance from immediate context. Dynamic windowing ensures sufficient data for stable estimation while adapting to season progression. Play-weighted aggregation improves signal-to-noise ratio by accounting for game-specific sample sizes. These primitives form a hierarchical structure where each layer refines the previous: opponent adjustment normalizes metrics, dynamic windows provide temporal adaptability, and play weights enhance robustness. The failure mode occurs when insufficient data exists for small windows or when opponent strength varies drastically without sufficient samples. Dualities emerge in how pass/rush EPA components interact with temporal smoothing—each requires distinct treatment due to differing play frequencies and strategic emphasis.
